messages:
Alex W: fyi ran a longctx perf sweep on staging, saw weird KV cache memory growth and hit-rate divergence after the kernel-selector change.
Jia L: can you paste the numbers? spike or steady growth?
Alex W: steady growth over ~10k requests with long-prefix prompts. mem used by kv-store went from 1.2GB -> 2.7GB over the run, p95 latency up ~18%.
Morgan: that sounds like fragmentation + under-eviction. Did the selector change alter attention chunking or KV page size?
Alex W: yes — new kernel packs goroutine batches differently which increases per-request KV allocations (smaller, more frequent). suspect more small entries and slab fragmentation.
Sam: do we have profiler traces? flamegraphs or allocation stacks?
Alex W: attached quick snapshot: heap profiles point to many ~512B entries from kv-key namespace "pref:session". reuse rate dropped from 88% -> 63% for common prefixes.
perf-bot: perf dashboard: https://perf.redwood/ci/1739999/longctx-kv-reuse (graph auto-attached)
Jia L: lower reuse suggests cache key mismatch across requests. Any change to key derivation or tenant salt?
Alex W: no tenant salt changes. but kernel reorder changed request batching boundaries; we now slice prefixes at different token offsets which mutated prefix fingerprints.
Morgan: aha. key design assumes prefix canonicalization to token boundary A, but batching moved to boundary B => same logical prefix hashed differently.
Sam: quick mitigation: normalize prefix canonicalization to text-level anchor before hashing (strip batch offsets). even a simple canonicalizer should recover reuse.
Alex W: prototyped a shim. config snippet:
```
kv.prefix_keyer:
  mode: canonical_text
  hash: xxh64
  anchor: sentence_boundary
  max_len: 1024
```
Alex W: with shim on, reuse went back to 85% and mem growth stabilized (1.3GB steady). p50 latency recovered ~12%.
Jia L: nice. long-term we should make cache key independent of kernel/batching decisions. keyer must run pre-batch.
Morgan: also consider a segmented-LRU with coalescing for tiny entries to reduce slab fragmentation. small-entry pooling would reduce allocator churn.
Sam: agree. propose a two-step plan: 1) short-term canonicalizer shim + hotpatch; 2) design SLRU + small-object pool + add unit tests that simulate batch boundary shifts.
Alex W: I'll open a canary PR for the shim and a perf canary job against the kernel-selector patchset.
perf-bot: canary created: PR #4217, Canary job queued.
Jia L: for observability, add a metric: cache_key_shape_changes_per_minute and per-prefix-fingerprint-variance.
Morgan: and add a regression test: run 10k synthetic requests with randomized batch boundaries and assert reuse >= 80% and memory growth < 0.2GB.
Sam: sounds good. also review eviction policy: current TTL heuristics might be too aggressive for longctx sessions; consider session-stickiness TTL bump for active sessions.
Alex W: noted. I'll include session affinity bump in the plan and measure unit-economics.
Alex W: tl;dr: regression introduced by kernel/batching boundary change -> mutated cache keys -> reuse drop -> fragmentation and mem growth. shortfix: canonicalize keys pre-batch. longfix: SLRU + small-entry pooling + stronger tests.
Jia L: thanks. ping me when PR is up and I'll help with the canary dashboard.
Sam: will follow up on eviction tuning.
perf-bot: incident-assist: none open. tagging: #kv-cache #longctx #perf-regression
